floor_history.headline: Recon s1: floor re-measured 32 (chassis unchanged, all WIP-imported verdicts spendable); $v0/$v1 exchange confirmed at .greg disposition level (pseudo 100 in $v1, 83/84/98 in $v0); frontier = instrume

Structural respelling dropped the honest floor 32 -> 14 and RETRACTS the s1 'RA exchange validated unreachable' verdict: every $v0/$v1 hunk inverse.py had foreclosed closed under ordinary shared-named

Structural session: honest floor 14 -> 2 and build_insns now 231 == target 231; duplicating the tail addend and the >>12 into both use_high arms (sanctioned duplicated-statement-into-arms, merged back

Permuter measured dead on the floor-2 residual (3 chassis, ~45 min, ~35k iters, zero sub-60 finds) and control-flow exit forms proven inert; in exchange the divergence is now pinned exactly to sched2'

Forensics RETRACTS s4's LUID-lock verdict: the LUID tie-break already yields target's order and is overridden by schedule_select's potential-hazard rule (sched.c:2707-2723); the chain's pri-47 is a $v

Forensics: the whole residual is ONE schedule_select potential-hazard override, proven to be a unit-class constant (F-B killed at source level), the block's priority lattice has no 46 and no 48-in-$v1

frontier.hypothesis: The ONLY surviving axis is making the 0x9C4 chain's quantity win local-alloc's qty_compare_1 sort so it takes $v0 (or is displaced to $a0) instead of $v1; then its WAR partner becomes the mult 105 / store 124 rather than insn 93, its whole chain inherits final_pri 48, it leaves the gp store's priority group, and schedule_select never compares them.
frontier.mechanism: local-alloc.c:1563 sorts quantities by floor_log2(qty_n_refs)*qty_n_refs*qty_size/(qty_death-qty_birth) DESCENDING and find_free_reg then takes the lowest free hard reg. Measured: chain-1 = 4*18/34 = 21176, chain-2 = 3*14/14 = 30000. Chain-1 must reach 30000 (refs > 25 at length 34, or length < 24 at refs 18, or chain-2's length > ~19 at refs 14); a tie also wins since qty_compare_1 breaks ties by lower qty number and chain-1 is qty 20 versus chain-2's 23.
frontier.next_probe: Sweep spellings that lengthen chain-2's live range or shorten chain-1's WITHOUT changing the instruction set - e.g. forms in which the final add ties to chain-2's pseudo rather than chain-1's (so the >>12 and the store hang off $v0), or in which an existing block value is made to overlap chain-2's 68..82 window. Grade every variant with `bash tools/wsl.sh 'bash tmp/grind/func_8001B748/s6/dump6.sh <src> <out>'` and read the blk=1 QTYDBG lines directly (win = the 0x9C4 chain's `got=` is 2 or 4, not 3), then confirm with PRIODBG SET final_pri >= 48 on its tail and the ABSENCE of a SELBEST line naming the gp store. Only then score.

frontier.hypothesis: Forcing the a+8 load off $v0 makes mult 105 read $v1, which hands the chain a pri-48 WAR partner without moving the chain out of $v1 at all - a strictly smaller perturbation than relocating the chain.
frontier.mechanism: The chain head is `(set (reg:SI 3 v1) (ashift:SI (reg/v:SI 17 s1) (const_int 2)))`; its priority is inherited from the last earlier insn that touches $v1, currently insn 93 at 47. If the mult's operand register were $v1 instead of $v0, the chain would anti-depend on mult 105 (pri 48) exactly as the 0x2710 chain anti-depends on store 124. The a+8 load's quantity is short-lived (QTYDBG birth 28 death 34) and takes $v0 purely by scan order because nothing occupies $v0 over that window.
frontier.next_probe: Find a spelling that keeps a value live in $v0 across the a+8 load's 28..34 window without adding an instruction - the natural candidate is arranging the dst+4 sum (insn 93, currently `v0 = v1 + t2` dying at store 98) to stay live one step longer, or changing which of the three store expressions consumes which mflo pair. Grade with QTYDBG (`got=` for the a+8 load quantity) before scoring; the sanctioned families in play are variable reuse and named-intermediate declaration order.

frontier.hypothesis: Putting the gp store in a DIFFERENT basic block from the chain removes the schedule_select comparison entirely, since schedule_select only ever ranks insns within one block's ready list.
frontier.mechanism: sched2 schedules block by block; two insns in different blocks are never in the same ready[]. s4 measured if/else, do-while(0), goto-end and inverted-guard spellings of the early-exit arm as byte-INERT (all score 2), but none of those created a block boundary BETWEEN the store and the chain - they only re-spelled the arm's entry/exit, and jump/jump2 folded them back into one block.
frontier.next_probe: Check the .jump2 dump (the pass that decides the final block structure) for the floor-2 base to see what would have to survive to split the arm, then look for a semantics-preserving form whose block boundary survives jump2 - and verify by counting `SCHEDDBG insn priorities:` block headers in the sched2 half of full.log (currently 19 blocks per pass; a win shows 20 with the store and the chain in different headers). If nothing survives jump2, kill this axis explicitly so s8 does not re-walk it.
